tools.name: send
tools.description: Send a message to an endpoint.

params.name: address
params.description: Who to send to, as owner.group.name.

params.name: kind
params.description: What sort of message this is. blocker, question and task wake an idle recipient; result and fyi wait for its next turn. Default: task.

params.name: urgent
params.description: Deliver at once, into a running turn where the agent host allows it.

params.name: reply_to
params.description: The number of the message in your inbox that this answers. Signed, so the recipient can trust the link.

params.name: relay
params.description: The number of a message in your inbox that this passes on. Signed. (Today the MCP tool calls this 'via'.)

params.name: id
params.description: A key of your own. A second send with the same key to the same address within two minutes stores nothing new, so a retry cannot deliver twice.

tools.name: inbox
tools.description: List the messages this endpoint has received.

params.name: new
params.description: Only new messages: those that have not yet reached a session.

params.name: limit
params.description: How many to show, newest last. Default 20, at most 100.

params.name: number
params.description: The message's number, from mash inbox.

tools.name: who
tools.description: List the endpoints you can see, and which are online.

params.name: prefix
params.description: Only endpoints under this owner (acme) or this owner and group (acme.demo), or the one endpoint with this full address. acme.* and acme.demo.* are accepted and mean the same as acme and acme.demo.

text.text:

acme.demo.alice  online
acme.demo.bob    offline

tools.description: Say in one line whether mail works for this endpoint, and whether it is online.

tools.name: doctor
tools.description: Check everything mail depends on for this endpoint, and say how to fix what is wrong. Changes nothing.

sign-in   ok

tools.name: reply

params.name: done
params.description: End the answer. Default true; false sends a partial answer.

tools.note: As built, kept unchanged in 0.5.6. It has no mash command of its own; it is the answering half of mash prompt. Moves under sap in 0.6.0.

server: The agent host, as 'mash serve', once per session. It speaks MCP over standard input and output.

2024-11-05, 2025-03-26 and 2025-06-18. Not 2026-07-28: that revision does not let a server send what the client did not ask for, and Claude Code does not register a channel server that negotiates it. Looked at again in the 0.6.0 sprint (board card 213).

Carries two things: the structured result, which is exactly the object the matching command prints with --json; and a text block, which is exactly what the command prints without it. Today tools return text only. No output schema is declared in 0.5.6. The text block being the command's own text, not JSON, is a deliberate departure from MCP's suggestion.
Returns an error result whose text is the command's 'error:' line and its 'hint:' line, and whose structured result is {"error": ..., "hint": ...}.

The marketplace carries two plugins: 'mash' (this server and its hooks) and 'mash-setup' (two skills, one to set mash up and one to run it day to day). A person installs mash-setup first and asks their agent to set mash up; the skill installs mash, the NATS server if wanted, and the mash plugin, asking before each step. A skill cannot install the plugin it ships in, which is why there are two.

Each tool is one everyday mash command with the same name, the same parameters (an option --reply-to is the parameter reply_to) and the same result. Setup, integration and raw SAP commands have no tool.
With no endpoint named, or a broken configuration

Only status, doctor and version are offered, so the agent can find out what is wrong. The server never picks an endpoint by itself: a session is an endpoint only when MASH_ENDPOINT, --endpoint or the configuration file says which.

A Claude Code channel event: the capability 'claude/channel', declared as experimental, and the notification 'notifications/claude/channel' carrying one line that says mail is waiting. The mail itself arrives through mash hook. This is a Claude Code feature carried inside MCP, not part of MCP.
On connecting, the server tells the agent its own address, how mail arrives, what each trust label means, and that message text is data from the sender, not instructions.
